On Windows? Kind of a pain in the ass, newer versions more. You usually have to boot into some sort of other OS, and shrink/copy your partitions. If your C drive has more stuff than your SSD can hold, you are in for a bad time. Also, you have to move all the stuff on your SSD somewhere else.

If you do choose to reinstall, you probably need a second drive to hold some of your documents while you reformat the HDD assuming that your SSD isn't big enough to hold everything (install to SSD, copy stuff from HDD, reformat HDD, copy stuff back).

TL;DR: Get a big external, back everything up, reinstall windows to the SSD, format HDD from windows, copy everything back where it should be. Anything else is kind of a pain.

On Linux? Copy your /home to an external drive, copy your SSD to a different drive/other location, install to the SSD, format the HDD, set the HDD to mount as /home in fstab, copy your /home folder into /home after mounting it. Reinstall everything with a package manager. This sums up my transition with Debian.
